sentences.text: Exemption allowed, subject to just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

This is a petition filed by the petitioners under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.315/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Kalindi Kunj, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned ASC appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

The brief facts of the case are that petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 24.08.2021 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife Gaurav Shivhare & Anr vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70419255/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 04.09.2021.
On 09.07.2022, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 15.03.2023 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, Delhi.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly,
the petition under Section 13B (2) of the HMA was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 05.04.2023 passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, South East, Saket Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, South East, Saket Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
5. Petitioners and SPA of respondent no.2 are present in Court and they have been identified by the IO.
Respondent no.2 has also joined the proceedings through video conferencing and has been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.

She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force,
pressure or coercion.

As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 2,90,000/- (bearing no.
769426 dated 15.05.2023 drawn on State Bank of India) has been handed over to the SPA of respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 10:59:50 question is quashed.
6. Learned ASC for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.315/2022,
under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Kalindi Kunj, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

8. It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioners that respondent no.1 has issued LOC against the petitioner no.1 and since the FIR has been quashed, LOC issued against the petitioner no.1 be also cancelled.
9. In view of the submissions of counsel for the petitioners, since the FIR has been quashed, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the LOC alive against the petitioner no.1.

Accordingly,
the LOC issued against the petitioner no.1 stands cancelled.
10. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
